Europe, 1936: one continent, one year, and the faces on this map were about to decide everything. Here's what was happening under the portraits.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ Germany: Hitler sent troops into the demilitarized Rhineland on 7 March, breaking Versailles and Locarno. He later admitted the army would have retreated if France had pushed back. France didn't.
2/ Italy: on 5 May Italian forces took Addis Ababa, and on 9 May Mussolini proclaimed an Italian empire from Rome. The League of Nations' sanctions had changed almost nothing.
3/ France: Léon Blum took office on 4 June as the first socialist and first Jewish prime minister. Within weeks his Popular Front passed the 40-hour week and two weeks of paid holidays.
4/ Britain: George V died in January, Edward VIII abdicated in December to marry Wallis Simpson, and George VI took the throne. PM Stanley Baldwin steered the whole crisis.
5/ Spain: on 17 July army officers launched a coup that became a civil war lasting until April 1939. Germany and Italy backed Franco; the USSR backed the Republic.
6/ Greece: PM Metaxas staged a self-coup on 4 August. USSR: Stalin's new constitution was adopted on 5 December. Turkey: Atatürk won back control of the Straits at Montreux.
7/ One year, half a dozen turning points. Which leader on this map do you think shaped the next decade most? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
